artifacts.summary: Design research for the no-record-versioning-in-deliverables rule, its taxonomy standard, and the shared record-version-patterns.sh library: parallels the sibling no-task-references triad, corrects a manifest.json provides.context wiring assumption, verifies the Verification repo's current (post-reorg) footprint, and proposes a durable-axis discrimination architecture with a blocking/advisory tiering rule.

next_steps: Run /plan 280 to create the implementation plan for the rule, taxonomy standard, and shared pattern library.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json, provides.context lists whole subdirectory names (e.g. "standards"), not individual file paths -- unlike provides.rules and provides.scripts, which are flat filename arrays. Before instructing a manifest.json edit to 'add a new context file to provides.context', check whether its parent directory is already listed; if so, no edit is needed.

shellcheck is not literally zero-finding (exit 0) on scripts/lib/task-reference-patterns.sh: it raises SC2034 'appears unused' on each exported pattern variable, because shellcheck cannot see an external source-time consumer. A sourced-only (Class C) library that exports variables for external consumers should add explicit '# shellcheck disable=SC2034' comments (precedented in scripts/skill-base.sh and others) to achieve a literal shellcheck-clean result, rather than assuming an un-annotated sibling file is the clean baseline.

When designing a regex-based detector that must discriminate a forbidden-language axis from a structurally similar but legitimate axis (e.g. record-versioning language vs. durable toolchain/schema/CI-cache version citations, both using bare vN tokens), prefer structural discriminators (dotted semver, @-prefixed pins, hyphen-embedded identifiers, known filename slugs) over a curated word list, and require co-occurrence of an ambiguous vocabulary word with the narrow token on the same line to escalate severity, rather than either blocking on the bare vocabulary word or ignoring it entirely. Validate the tiering choice against a real corpus before finalizing -- in one cross-check, bare 'supersedes' and bare past-tense vocabulary (no longer/previously/formerly) both occurred pervasively in legitimate, already-accepted prose with zero relation to the forbidden pattern.
